model: Dedicated Controls (CU 361 / CU 362) with CIM 200 / CIM 260 / CIM 500 (Modbus)
applies_to: Grundfos Dedicated Controls wastewater pit controller (CU 361 / CU 362, up to six pumps and a mixer) with a CIM 200 Modbus RTU, CIM 260 cellular or CIM 500 Modbus TCP module; functional profile 98393520 (2023-03).
summary: Grundfos Dedicated Controls runs wastewater lift stations with up to six pumps, a mixer, level sensors or float switches. A CIM module in the CU 36X makes it a Modbus slave with blocks for pit control, pit status, pit data and one 50-register block per pump. This map covers pit commands and level setpoints, operating mode and per-pump state bits, pit level, flows, energy and overflow counters, and the main per-pump data (run hours, starts, current, power, frequency).

addressing.note: Registers are printed as 5-digit register numbers; this manual states that register X is addressed as X - 1 in the telegram (e.g. 00301 PitWaterLevel is wire address 300). Pump n's block starts at 00401 + 50 x (n-1).

source.title: Modbus for Dedicated Controls - CIM 200 Modbus RTU, CIM 260 3G/4G Cellular, CIM 500 Ethernet for Modbus TCP - Functional profile and user manual
source.pages: p. 18 (block overview, 32-bit rule), pp. 19-20 (CIM blocks), pp. 22-34 (pit control and status), pp. 35-38 (pit data, pump 1), pp. 39-48 (pumps 2-6), pp. 68-70 (telegrams)

notes: The manual states that 32-bit values are split into registers ending HI and LO and recombined as HI x 65536 + LO, so they are ABCD.
All registers can be read with function 03 or 04; they are listed as holding registers. 0xFFFF means not available (missing sensor or option).
Pumps 2-6 repeat the pump 1 layout at +50 registers each (00451, 00501, 00551, 00601, 00651); this was checked against the printed pump 2-6 tables.

Left out: per-pump alarm/warning words (004x23-004x28, 004x41-004x42), sensor presence and setpoint-select fields, the pit sensor-presence and float-switch 5 registers (00223-00240), most user-defined counters, the real-time clock split registers, the hour log, event log and data log blocks, and the name string. Bit meanings of PitAlarms/PitWarnings are in section 11.11 of the manual and are not decoded here.
Level and set-level registers are in 0.01 m; writing the Set...Level registers (00121-00137) changes the controller's configured levels.
Left out: GrinderReverseCounter (00389-00390), because the pit status table also prints 00389 for PitWarnings5, so the number is not unambiguous in this edition.
Pumps 2-6 print the current asymmetry register as PumpNAsym, while pump 1 uses Pump1iAsym; the names are kept as printed.

integration.summary: Poll 00203 (operating mode), 00206/00209 (pumps running / in alarm) and 00301 (pit level) for the station overview, and each pump block for run hours, starts and current. Use PitControl 00101 to reset alarms, interlock the pit or return it to Auto, and 00103-00108 to force pumps on or off.
integration.enable: Fit the CIM module in the CU 36X; set the address and speed on its switches (CIM 200). Remote control needs write access: if SCADA PIN protection is on, write the PIN to 00109 first and check PitStatus bit 5.
quirks: Control bits act on a rising edge; with AutoAckControlBits = 1 (default) the CIM clears them itself.
InterlockPit (00101 bit 3) stops all pumps for the time in SetInterlockTimeout (00111, minutes); the pit then returns to Auto by itself.
setup: CIM 200 default: 19200 baud, even parity, 1 stop bit; SW3 selects no parity with 2 stop bits.
CIM 500: select Modbus TCP on the rotary switch; port 502.
gotchas: A changed RegisterOffset (00002) moves every register above 00100.
Most flow, energy and overflow values need the matching sensor (flow meter, MP 204, level sensor) or read 0xFFFF.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
